turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I've put you in room two. Before you came through I took his blood pressure, one hundred and thirty-eight over eighty-four, and his pulse was seventy-six.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lovely, thanks. Come sit, both of you. How have you been keeping, really?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Fine.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ag, he's not fine. We came for the repeat script, but he wants a stronger painkiller. The knee is sore the whole time.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Shame, man. Tell me about that knee, wherever you want to start.
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Right.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): The right one. What does it feel like when it's bad?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Sore.

[SEG0009] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The right knee has been sore the whole time, about three months, since he helped my brother shift a fridge. Walking to the shop and the stairs make it worse. If he sits with the leg up it eases a bit.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any swelling, or does it give way under you?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Swollen.
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Puffy by the evening, ja. It doesn't give way. He hasn't fallen, touch wood.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain, or shortness of breath?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): And dizziness, or feeling faint with the tablets?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. What are you actually using for the pain these days?
[SEG0018] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Panado. He keeps on about Tramacet, the stuff his brother got from the chemist, because he says the Panado isn't touching it.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): How are you taking the Panado?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Three.
[SEG0021] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Well, actually I thought it was twice a day, um, no, sorry, he's right, three times a day after food. Two tablets, five hundred milligrams each time.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the everyday ones, the sugar tablets and the water tablet?
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The sugar tablets, that's the Glucophage, morning and night. The little water tablet is for his high blood pressure. He's diabetic, hey, a long time.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you know the strengths?
[SEG0025] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The sugar ones are five hundred milligrams, one in the morning and one at night. The water tablet, I couldn't tell you the number on the box.

[SEG0026] person_1 (NURSE): The pharmacy list here says metformin, the Glucophage, eight hundred and fifty milligrams twice a day. The water tablet is hydrochlorothiazide, twelve point five milligrams in the morning.
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's not what's in our cupboard. I've been giving him the five hundreds. I don't know where eight fifty comes from.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, we won't guess. Are you taking those sugar tablets every day, the way they're written?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the purple inhaler, are you still using that for your chest?
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The purple one, ja. He can never remember the name. A puff when the chest feels tight, not every day.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Sometimes.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any medicine allergies I should know about?
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me feel that knee. It's warm, a bit puffy over the right knee, tender on the inner side, and it bends all the way.
[SEG0036] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So can he still have the Tramacet? His brother says it's harmless.

[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): I hear both of you. With the diabetes and the high blood pressure, I'm not going to prescribe Tramacet or any stronger painkiller today. I think this is your old knee arthritis grumbling, not a pain that needs codeine. Those mixes can make you dizzy and constipated.
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Why?

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Because the safer plan is to keep the Panado properly, two five-hundreds three times a day with food, and you can rub Voltaren gel on the knee three times a day. Don't double the Panado if it's still sore.
[SEG0040] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And which sugar dose do we follow, the five hundred or the eight fifty?

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Don't change it yourself. Keep giving what's in the cupboard until I phone. I'll ask the pharmacy to confirm which metformin strength is actually his before the next box goes out.
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): Okay.
[SEG0043] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The bakkie was making a racket this morning, that's why we were late, sorry. His brother will moan that you said no.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): No stress about the bakkie. Come back in three months for the next script review. If the knee swells up more or you can't walk on it, come sooner.
[SEG0045] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the repeat at the front for the Panado and the water tablet, and I'll hold the sugar tablets until pharmacy confirms the dose.
[SEG0046] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, thank you.
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): Thanks.

spec.situation: Routine repeat-prescription review at a small clinic with a pharmacy technician present; patient wants a stronger painkiller; tablet names and doses are discussed in detail, one dose is read from the pharmacy list and differs from the patient's own; doctor declines the stronger medicine.
features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

bad.reason: Medication, dose, frequency, and indication are supported, but hydrochlorothiazide details came from nurse, not family member.
bad.text: water tablet (generic_name=hydrochlorothiazide, dose=12.5 mg, frequency=in the morning, indication=high blood pressure, status=currently_used, reported_by=family_member)

bad.reason: Diabetes and long duration are supported, but duration was reported by family member, not doctor.

omissions.text: Dizziness/feeling faint with the tablets was asked about and was not clearly denied; patient answered 'Sometimes, not really,' indicating possible intermittent dizziness rather than absence.
